newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia king pardons dissident Khmer Rouge leader.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king pardons dissident Khmer Rouge leader.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk on Saturday pardoned dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary for his role in the guerilla group's "killing fields" reign in the late 1970s, one of the country's two co-premiers said.
"His majesty the king signed the amnesty before 11 o'clock this morning with the support of two thirds of (the members of) parliament," Second Prime Minister Hun Sen told Reuters.

Hun Sen said it had been easy to collect the signatures of two-thirds of the nation's 120 MPs as he and first Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh were leaders of the two main parties, the Cambodian People's Party and the prince's FUNCINPEC party.

Ranariddh and Hun Sen went to the palace shortly after 10.00 a.m. (0300 GMT) to discuss their earlier written request to the king to grant an amnesty to Ieng Sary, who was foreign minister during Pol Pot's brutal 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime when more than one million people died.

The premiers wanted amnesty for Ieng Sary, who split from Khmer Rouge hardliners in early August, in the interests of national reconciliation. The king had said he would only consider an amnesty on receiving written requests from the governnment and a two-thirds majority of parliament.

Ieng Sary, who was sentenced to death in absentia for his role in the genocide during the 1975-79 Khmer Rouge reign, denied on Monday that he was involved in any killings and said the government should sort out his legal status in order for peace talks to advance.
